name: Black Banners
description:
Black Banners

Quick Reference

Tagline: A contract is only as good as the next settlement — but loyalty is earned in blood, not silver.

Banner-Captain (Elite):

“A contract is only as good as the next payday, and a grudge is only as sharp as the sword backing it. In this game, we sell steel by the season and vendettas by the year. But a captain who forgets the men in the mud won't last the winter.”

Veteran Sergeant (Commoner):

“I've seen three captains rise and fall in the time it takes to grow a beard. The mud stays the same. The pay comes when it pleases. But the men? They remember who shared their fire and who ate alone. Keep your blade sharp and your word sharper. The camp sings? You live. They stop singing? Even the best charter bleeds.”

Genre / Mood: Mercenary realism, winter warfare, logistics-driven violence, loyalty in the mud.

System Type: Portable overlay — apply to any region (Acasia, Violet Steppe, Ecktorian borderlands). Not a fixed geography.

Condotta & Crowns

Ecktorian treasuries bankroll a perpetual border-war they claim to be containing. In truth, the gold keeps the fire burning. The Black Banners are mercenary leagues — ex-Utaran legionaries, second-sons, deserters, and exiles — who sell steel to the highest bidder, today's ally becoming tomorrow's quarry. Between them move the Ykrul steppe-clans (swift, pragmatic, oath-canny) and the Vilikari hill tribes (crafty, patient, and proud). Ecktorian ministers call it “pressure management.” The companies call it a season — and a season is measured in the rhythm of pay, but also in snowdrifts, broken wheels, and the weight of a dead friend's shield.

What you notice first: The smell of wet wool and old blood. The way every tent has a roster pinned to its flap — and beside it, a list of the fallen. The silence when the chest is opened — and the murmur when it's light. The way veterans watch the horizon not for enemies, but for the supply train.

The one rule that kills newcomers: Never break a Bell Dawn. Three bells at sunrise means bury the dead, trade prisoners, fix the wells, no ambushes. Violating it is how legends end badly — and how captains end hanging. The dead don't forget.

The Ninth Taboo Manifestation

In any mercenary camp, the ninth tent in a row collapses before dawn. The ground beneath is always damp, as if something rose from below and left. Those who sleep in that tent wake with no memory of the night — but a new name carved into their belt buckle. The name is never theirs.

The Theater of Banners

Here, war is a marketplace — but also a forge, a campfire, a brotherhood of mud and steel. The Black Banners are not a single army but a squabbling league of freelance violence, bound by camp law, customs of compensation, and the shared knowledge that tomorrow's enemy might be today's employer. The real battles are fought in tents over agreements; the clash outside is just the review. Loyalty is a bond that shifts with circumstance — but it also lives in the sergeant who shares his last ration, the surgeon who works through the night, the captain who stands in the shield wall.

Between the rigid honor codes of Ecktorian nobility and the fluid pragmatism of steppe clans and hill tribes, mercenaries navigate a dangerous middle ground. Survival depends on knowing when to keep an oath and when to break one — always at dawn, with a witness, and with surety paid. But it also depends on knowing whose back to watch, whose flask to share, and whose name to call when the snow closes in.

Names of the Black Banners

Mercenary names are often aliases, nicknames from past campaigns, or the color of a faded banner. Surnames are rare; epithets are everything.

Quickstart (Two-Minute Setup)

  1. Condotta Crossroads: Put two conflicting charters on the table. Ask: Who do you disappoint first?
  2. Company Sheet: Name, Colors, Captain. Add timers: Payday [4], Supplies [4], Cohesion [6].
  3. Pressure Timers: Pick two external threats (e.g., Skirmish Spiral [6], Camp Fever [6], Winter Deepens [6]).
  4. Allegiances in Flux: At each scene start, roll 1d6 and apply the twist (see table).
  5. Honor vs. Pragmatism Dial: Slide based on choices; affects Position, logistics, and how the men remember you.

The Four-Suit Generator

Draw until you have all four suits. Highest rank sets the main Timer (2–5 $$ 4, 6–10 $$ 6, J/Q/K $$ 8, A $$ 10). Any Ace echoes winter & loyalty motifs: hunger, omen, promotion-by-attrition, or a sudden blizzard that buries both sides.

Spades — Places (Camps, Battlefields, Fortresses)

9Command TentMaps show borders diplomacy erased. `[SOCIAL]` A player who studies the map for a scene may ask one question about enemy intentions; on a Miss, the map is a decoy — start False Orders [4]. The tent smells of fear and bad wine.
10Watch-TowerStacked from skulls and slate; crows know the countersign. `[WAR]` The crows will warn of ambush once, but only if fed a memory (erase a minor fact). The watchman never sleeps.
JAncient March-KeepHeld by a skeleton garrison of veterans; they remember when banners were gold. `[DEATH]` They will fight for you if you swear an oath to restore their banner — start Oath Share [6]. Their captain has no shadow.
QThe Bone FieldsYkrul elders parley among cairns; reckon oaths with the dead. `[DEATH]` `[OATH]` The dead vote on any dispute. Roll Spirit+Lore (DV 4). On success, they side with you (gain +1 Position on next parley). On failure, they demand a blood-price. The wind carries their voices.
KMarcher's FortressThree walls, two sieges' scars, one gate that opens inward only. `[COMBAT]` The gate opens inward so the dead can leave. Living who enter without permission take Harm 1 (spiritual backlash). The stones weep when an agreement is broken.
AThe Singing WastesFallen weapons hum with voices of their last wielders. `[MAGIC]` `[DEATH]` Each weapon can answer one question about its owner's death. After three questions, the Wastes awaken — start Wrath of the Fallen [8]. The song is a lament.

Hearts — People & Factions

Rank

NameDescription Mechanical Hook
2Young CadetFather's sword, mother's share, hunger to prove himself. `[SOCIAL]` If you mentor him (a downtime scene), he becomes a Cap 1 follower. If you ignore him, he joins a rival company — tick Rival Agenda +1. He has never seen a man die.
3Veteran SergeantCounts scars like medals; spends them on whiskey and mercy. `[COMBAT]` `[SOCIAL]` She will fight for you, but at end of scene demands a story about a battle you survived. If you cannot provide one, she takes a button from your coat — a promise.
4Ecktorian Banner-CaptainGriffon standard, roster of noble grudges, smile like winter. `[LAW]` He offers a Letter of Marque (once: ignore one legal complication). Accepting starts his Favor Share [4] — he will call in a favor during a critical moment. His boots are always clean.
5Condotta BrokerChanges colors when wind turns, always lands on his feet. `[SOCIAL]` He will flip a contract for you — but the price is a Black Mark (reputation stain). He has three names and uses none.
6Ykrul Clan EmissarySpeaks in riddled proverbs; pays in copper from a cursed mine. `[SOCIAL]` `[OATH]` He offers a Safe-Conduct Token (one free passage through Ykrul land). Accepting marks Obligation [2] — the horse you ride will remember.
7Vilikari War-Chief's Second SonHonor burns brighter than his father's patience. `[SOCIAL]` He will join your next battle as a Cap 2 ally, but if he takes Harm, start a Blood Feud [6] with his clan. His axe has a name.
8Surgeon of the Red TallyTreats friend and foe; her record balances in blood. `[SHARE]` She can heal 1 Harm — but the patient's name is added to her roll. Once per arc, she calls in the share: a dangerous mission. Her hands never shake.
9QuartermasterKnows where every coin went and every man will fall. `[SHARE]` His bribe book is thicker than his roster. Spend 1 Boon to cancel one Supplies tick — but he now has a String on you. He never eats with the men.
10Tribune's Aide-de-CampSealed orders contradict the general's intent. `[SOCIAL]` He will leak the real orders for a Favor Share [4] — but the leak may be a trap. His seal ring is warm.
JThe Black ColonelLegendary commander not seen in months, yet his banner rides. `[LEGEND]` The banner rides alone. If you follow it, you find a cache (gain 1 Diamond of your choice). Following it three times summons his ghost. He never lost a battle — only his way home.
QYkrul Clan-MotherWeaves war-braids from hair of oath-breakers. `[OATH]` She can witness any oath; breaking it gives her power over you (she may demand a service). Her braids have nine knots.
KVilikari High ChiefTrades mercenaries like game pieces; never tips the board. `[SOCIAL]` He offers a Trading Charter (buy/sell anything in any camp). Using it ticks Cohesion +1 (soldiers suspect you of corruption). His smile is an agreement.
AThe Bannerless OneCommands loyalty without rank or flag. `[LEGEND]` She appears when the camp is darkest. She clears one segment of the pay cycle — but you incur a Price of Mercy [4]. When it fills, she asks for a prisoner — or a promise. Her face is never the same twice.

2Payday DelayedSupplies dwindle before coin arrives. `[SHARE]` Tick Payday +1. On fill, a squad deserts — lose 1 Supplies and gain a Black Mark. The captain blames the weather.
3False OrdersYour target is now your ally — on paper. `[SOCIAL]` The first command this scene is misinterpreted unless countered with a Diamond (cipher, cantor, witness). The messenger's hands are clean.
4Blizzard PinsTwo rival companies, one cloister; vows and knives both come out. `[WEATHER]` `[COMBAT]` Tick Cohesion +1. The abbot will sell safe passage to the highest bidder — start an Auction [4] timer. The snow is red by dawn.
5Ykrul Counter-OfferBetter terms than Ecktoria; your contract becomes a liability. `[SOCIAL]` `[SHARE]` You may accept (gain +1 Effect, mark Obligation [2]) or refuse (tick the pay timer +1). The horses watch you decide.
6Condotta FlipUnit switches colors mid-battle; your “relief” hits your flank. `[COMBAT]` On a Miss, the unit attacks you. On a Partial, they demand double compensation — tick Payday +1. Their old banner burns in your camp.
7Camp FeverBlooms in the surgeon's tent; the counting-house for the dead. `[DEATH]` Start Camp Fever [4]. Each failed Endurance test ticks it. At 4, a key NPC dies. The surgeon weeps in silence.
8Vilikari RaidCuts your supply road; winter moves the schedule. `[COMBAT]` `[TRAVEL]` Tick Supplies +1. The raiders left a recipe — cooking it gives 1 Supplies but starts a Rival Hunt [4] (they want the recipe back). The stew tastes of revenge.
9Honor Code CollisionEcktorian ideals vs. mercenary pragmatism; the camp splits by doctrine. `[SOCIAL]` Choose Honor (tick Supplies +1, logistics suffer) or Pragmatism (gain +1 Effect now, but start Parley Divided [4]). The men watch which way you lean.
10Tribune CapturedThe aide must choose: the rescue or the war. `[SOCIAL]` `[SHARE]` Rescue him: lose 1 Supplies. Abandon him: gain Black Mark but tick the pay timer –1 (his captors compensate you). His ghost will remember.
JBlack Colonel's BannerAppears on the wrong field; confusion is a weapon. `[COMBAT]` Roll 1d6. On 1–3, the enemy believes you have reinforcements (+1 Position). On 4–6, your own side hesitates (–1 die on first attack). The banner has no shadow.
QBlood-FeastClan-Mother calls it; all contracts suspended until dawn's judgment. `[OATH]` `[SOCIAL]` The feast is a trial. Each PC must confess a broken oath or take Harm 1 (the clan judges). The meat is always fresh.
KHigh Chief's GamePlays companies against each other; “winner” takes obligations, not spoils. `[SOCIAL]` `[SHARE]` The “winner” inherits a Obligation Timer [6] from the loser. Refusing the game starts a Vendetta [4]. The game has no rules — only winners.
AThe Singing Wastes AwakenEvery fallen blade rises to seek its last hand. `[MAGIC]` `[DEATH]` The blades attack everyone for 1 round. Afterward, any PC may claim a Cursed Blade (+1 die, but the blade whispers secrets — the GM gains 1 SB per scene). The song is a scream.

Diamonds — Treasures & Discoveries

Each Diamond is a physical object with a cost and expiration.

JField Promotion WarrantAssume command of a shattered unit, inherit its timers. `[AUTHORITY]` `[SHARE]` You gain a Cap 2 follower (the unit's sergeant), but inherit their pay timer [2/4] and Black Mark [1]. The sergeant has seen too much.
QClan-Mother's War-BraidsHer chosen fight beside you this battle, then judge you after. `[COMBAT]` `[SOCIAL]` Gain a Cap 3 ally for one battle. Afterward, she judges your conduct — on a Miss, she takes a war-braid from you (lose 1 Boon). The braid is warm.
KHigh Chief's Trading CharterBuy or sell anything in any camp, no questions asked aloud. `[TRADE]` Once per arc, treat a market roll as Clean Success. The questions are asked in silence — the answers are compensated in silence (GM gains 1 SB). The charter is written on skin.

They fight for one scene without tracking the pay timer or cohesion. Afterward, the word is forgotten — you cannot use it again. The men will not speak of it.

Company Mechanics (Visible Tracks)

Every mercenary company (PC-led or NPC) tracks three timers:

  • Payday [4] – Missed compensation, bad terms, seized chests. On fill: a squad deserts (lose 1 Supplies) or a veteran sells secrets (GM gains 2 SB). The men whisper.
  • Supplies [4] – Weather, marches, sabotage. While Supplies $$ 3, all risky maneuvers start Position –1 unless you bring a Diamond (scavenge, requisition). Hunger is a slow knife.
  • Cohesion [6] – Losses, betrayals, officer feuds. When Cohesion hits 1–2, the GM may convert the first 1 SB each scene into Desertion, Brawl, or Refusal. Trust is the first casualty.

Recovery: A successful Payline Drill scene clears 1 Payday. A Quartermaster Audit clears 1 Supplies. A Rally & Reform roll (Presence+Command, DV 3) clears 1 Cohesion. Shared hardship binds faster than coin.

Camp Event Mini-Generator (d8)

When the company makes camp or when tensions run high, roll on this table for a camp event that affects morale, cohesion, or supplies.

|p0.85|}

d8

Event
1Deserter's Tale. A soldier tries to flee with a payroll satchel. If caught, the company demands a public flogging. Intervening costs 1 Boon but earns a loyalty share (+1 Cohesion). If ignored, tick Payday +1 (the coin is gone) and Cohesion –1 (trust erodes). The deserter's name is scratched from the roll.
2Surgeon's Lottery. The camp surgeon runs a lottery for medical priority. Those who pay 1 Boon jump the queue. Those who refuse may lose a wounded ally to infection (lose 1 Supplies or a follower). The surgeon's ledger grows longer — and her smile thinner.
3Muster of the Fallen. A ghostly formation marches through camp at midnight. Veterans take it as an omen. Each PC must test Resolve (DV 3) or gain the Haunted condition (–1 die on initiative for one day). On a success, they gain +1 die on the next morale check. The dead are counting.
4Brawl Over Bread. A fight erupts over the last rations. The quartermaster demands the party intervene. Choose: Break it up (costs 1 Fatigue, no change), Take sides (gain a small faction's favor but tick Cohesion –1), or Let it burn (lose 1 Supplies to spoilage). The loser's face stays in the mud.
5Pardoner's Visit. A traveling pardoner offers absolutions for past sins. Pay 1 Boon to clear one Black Mark (the pardoner writes your name in his book). Refuse, and the pardoner's curse gives –1 Position on the next social roll against clergy. His book has many names.
6Desertion Ring. An informant reveals a plot to desert en masse. The party can pay arrears (clear 1 Payday), execute the ringleaders (gain a Black Mark but tick Cohesion +1), or ignore it (tick Payday +2 as half the camp vanishes overnight). The informant wants a horse.
7Camp-Fever Peak. The surgeon's tent overflows. Mark 1 Fatigue for each PC. A successful Medicine test (DV 4) reduces the effect by half. On a critical failure, a key NPC (the quartermaster or a sergeant) dies. The fever has a name.
8The Bannerless One Visits. The mysterious figure appears at the edge of the firelight. She offers to clear 2 pay cycle segments in exchange for a Price of Mercy [4] timer. The timer advances each time the party shows mercy to an enemy. When full, she asks for a prisoner — or a promise. Her eyes are old.

Allegiances in Flux (Scene Start, 1d6)

At the start of every scene involving mercenaries, roll 1d6:

  1. Condotta Flip – Rival charter offers better terms. Accept: gain Black Mark [1] with old patron. Refuse: tick Payday +1. The ink is still wet.
  2. Ykrul Counter-offer – Accept an exit-rich but costly route: gain +1 Effect now, mark Obligation [2]. Refuse: tick Payday +1. The wind shifts.
  3. Vilikari Shortcut – +1 Effect on this maneuver via night roads; GM gains 1 SB (hostile terrain later). The path is older than the kingdom.
  4. Ecktorian “Correction” – March under “imperial guidance”: +1 Position this scene or take a Black Mark for defiance. The seal is heavy.
  5. False Orders – First command this scene suffers misinterpretation unless countered with a Diamond (cipher, cantor, witness). The messenger's hands are clean.
  6. Bannerless One – A myth-wrapped figure clears 1 pay segment – but starts Price of Mercy [2]. When it fills, she asks for a prisoner you'd rather keep. She was always there.

Honor vs. Pragmatism Dial

Place a two-step dial. Starting position: balanced (0).

  • Honor (left): +1 Position in parley/oathbound actions; logistics burn faster (increase Supplies by 1 on a Partial where you'd normally be safe). The old songs approve.
  • Pragmatism (right): +1 Effect in ambush/sabotage; social rolls start one step worse Position when oaths/witnesses matter. The men learn to watch their backs.

Centering Actions: Settle arrears on-screen, return prisoners with witness, fulfill a broken writ at cost. Move the dial one step toward center. The campfire remembers.

Black Banners Superstitions (burn for +1 die once)

  • Bread to the Bell: Crumble a crust at a camp's bell post. Ignore the first Payday Delayed penalty. [SUPERSTITION]
  • Knot the Roster: Tie a single knot in the company roster. Cancel Condotta Flip or take –1 die on your next negotiation (your choice). [SUPERSTITION]
  • Name to the Mud: Whisper a dead captain's name into the latrine trench. Gain +1 Effect when rallying the company this scene, but mark Obligation to the Bannerless One. [SUPERSTITION]

Pursuit Ladder (Near / Mid / Far)

  • Advance/Withdraw (Wits + Ride or Stealth): On a hit, shift one band. On a strong hit, also impose Dust Cloud (cover retreat).
  • Cut the Contract (Presence + Sway): On a hit, freeze range for one exchange; if a Condotta Rider's Pass is in your possession, +1 die.
  • Weather the Blizzard (Endurance + Survival): On a hit in Blizzard Pins, you pick who finds shelter; on a miss, the GM does.

Boss Seeds (Three-Phase Foes)

  • The Coin-Captain (Mercenary Turncoat) — Phases: Fair Offer $$ Betrayal Clause $$ Payday Massacre. Cracks: expose his dual contract before the company, pay off his debt to the Condotta Broker, or outbid him for his own loyalty.
  • The Quartermaster-Provost (Logistics Tyrant) — Phases: Supply Freeze $$ Ration Cuts $$ Starvation Siege. Cracks: steal his secret ledger, rally the men with a shared meal (spend 1 Supplies), or break his control of the supply route.
  • The Singing Wakes (Weapon-Host) — Phases: Whisper $$ Chorus $$ Scream. Cracks: perform the Three Silencing Acts (funeral honors for a fallen blade, bury a broken standard, ring the wind-break bell).

GM Tools

Field Procedures

  • Colors & Countersigns: Declaring correct countersigns cancels the first False Orders SB each night; wrong signs worsen Position on first contact.
  • Payline Drill: If a scene depicts orderly compensation, clear 1 Payday. If pay is “creative,” clear it but mark Black Mark – future officers begin one step colder in parley.
  • Scavenge Doctrine: After battles, gain 1 temporary Gear tag or advance Supplies by 1; on a 1–2 on 1d6, spawn “Honor vs. Pragmatism” conflict immediately.

Cross-Regional Use

  • Vhasia: A Condotta Rider's Pass substitutes for a Safe-Conduct on the Pont-du-Tithe once; after use, start a Parlement Divided tick.
  • Viterra: A Ykrul Safe-Conduct Token may be notarised as Ferry Priority; the notary's fee is a story.
  • Ubral: A Clan-Mother's War-Braid counts as a Guest-Token in hill-forts; the clans will ask whose side you took.
  • Mistlands: A Banner-Captain's Seal can be presented to a Bell-Warden as proof of lawful passage; the Warden tests it with a bell. If it rings false, the mist takes a day.
  • Valewood: A Field Promotion Warrant can be offered to a Green Knight as proof of worth; the Knight may challenge you to a trial of paths instead of blades.
Patronage & Power

In the Black Banners, power flows through agreements, coin chests, and the weight of a reputation — but also through the sergeant who knows each man's name, the cook who stretches the rations, the smith who works through the night. A Banner-Captain's authority rests on the number of companies he commands; a Condotta Broker's on the thickness of his roster. Yet loyalty is not bought — it is earned in the mud, at the latrine, across a shared fire.

For the GM:

Power in the Black Banners is measured in payday timers, broker's favors, and the length of a duel record — but also in the camp's mood, the quartermaster's ledger, and the stories the veterans tell. Patronage often takes the form of dual contracts, emergency requisitions, or the Bannerless Word – each tied to a specific company, broker, or share. To emphasize the mercenary realism:

  • Use the pay and supply timers as visible pressure. Let players negotiate, raid, or pledge future services to clear ticks.
  • Enforce Allegiances in Flux – every scene, loyalties may shift. The Keeper's SB pool grows when the party breaks an agreement.
  • Let Honor vs. Pragmatism be a dial the party can slide through their actions. Center it by a costly act of mercy or a profitable betrayal.
  • Track Black Marks as a persistent reputation score. Three Black Marks and no condotta broker will write a clear agreement for you.
  • Remember the human element: the soldier who shares his last ration, the captain who stands in the line, the surgeon who weeps in private. These are the ties that outlast coin.

In the Black Banners, the camp sings when pay arrives — and falls silent when the coin chest is empty. But the camp also sings when a wounded friend survives, when the supply train arrives, when the snow melts and the road opens. The song is never just about coin.

Final GM Mantra (Black Banners Edition)

The camp sings when pay arrives — and falls silent when the chest is empty. Set DV low. Use Allegiances in Flux every scene. Let Payday, Supplies, and Cohesion be visible. Spend SB as false orders, cut supply lines, or camp fever. And remember: in the Black Banners, a broken agreement costs more than a broken blade — but a broken trust costs more than either.
